title: RBI holds 84% of India's gold reserves domestically - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
FILE PHOTO: The Reserve Bank of India held 880.52 metric tonnes of gold at September-end, with 740.13 tonnes stored domestically. | Photo Credit: BURKINA FASO PRESIDENCY

The Indian central bank ​further increased its domestic gold ‌holdings, even as the ​yellow metal's overall ⁠share of reserves slipped as of end-September, data released on ‌Wednesday showed.

The Reserve Bank of India ‌held 880.52 metric ‌tonnes ⁠of gold as part ⁠of its foreign exchange reserves as of September-end, a half-yearly ​report released ‌by it showed.

Of this, 740.13 metric tonnes, or 84%, of gold ‌reserves were held domestically and ​140.39 metric tonnes were with the ⁠Bank of England and the Bank for International ‌Settlements.

India has been steadily bringing back gold reserves onshore over the past two years as geopolitical risks rose.

In ‌March, the proportion of ​these reserves held locally was 77%.

The share of ⁠gold in total foreign ⁠exchange reserves decreased to 14.38% as of ‌September from 16.7% six months ago.
